references.text: The prophet Isaiah uses the image of a bridegroom in connection with God's relationship to his people, which can be seen as a precursor to Jesus' use of the bridegroom metaphor to describe his relationship with his disciples.
The prophet Joel speaks of a time of joy and celebration, comparable to the time when the bridegroom is present, a time without fasting, which Jesus refers to.
The prophet Hosea also uses the image of a bridegroom in connection with God's relationship to Israel, reflecting Jesus' use of the bridegroom metaphor.
Matthew gives a parallel account to Mark 2:19, where Jesus uses the same metaphor about the bridegroom to explain why his disciples do not fast.
Luke includes a similar account to Mark 2:19, where Jesus explains why his disciples do not fast by using the bridegroom metaphor.
